references.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks

facts: RAG retrieves relevant external information and supplies it as context for generating answers.
A typical pipeline prepares documents, retrieves passages for a question, and generates using those passages.
Chunking splits documents into smaller pieces. Embeddings represent meaning as numerical vectors. Vector stores support similarity search; keyword retrieval is also possible.
Using RAG does not inherently require retraining model weights.
Retrieval can miss relevant evidence; evidence can be outdated; generated answers can still be wrong.
Citations support verification but do not guarantee correctness. Missing evidence should lead to abstention rather than invented facts.
College timetable and shop policy examples are fictional teaching examples, not claims about real institutions.
